claims.text: The apply.md page cross-references the page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ (titled 'Output value errors'), which must exist in the docs.

When an Output is treated as a plain value (e.g., string-interpolated), Pulumi produces placeholder text like `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` in log lines, generated files, or resource properties instead of the actual value.
The 'Output value errors' troubleshooting page covers this and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
Resources created inside an `apply` will not appear in `pulumi preview` unless the output's value is already known, so preview output may not match the actual changes when `pulumi up` is run.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ exists and covers errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
In Pulumi, stringifying, branching on (e.g., using in conditionals), or reading an Output value as if it were a plain value produces errors.
Pulumi Cloud returns the error '409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress' when an update is already in progress on a stack.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors.

The troubleshooting sub-pages update-conflicts, server-errors, post-step-errors, connection-issues, destroy-failures, interrupted-updates, and architecture-mismatch exist under /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/.

The Pulumi CLI produces a `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` error when it cannot access a self-managed (DIY) state backend, and the DIY backend docs page has an 'error-reading-pulumimetayaml' anchor documenting it.
On Apple Silicon Macs, running x86_64 binaries under Rosetta 2 can cause Pulumi crashes or hangs.
`pulumi destroy` can fail in some scenarios.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
The Pulumi CLI supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
Pulumi provides automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging for debugging and diagnostics.
Pulumi offers pre-release dev builds that can be installed to access bug fixes that haven't shipped in a stable release yet.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
The logging guide at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/ has an 'automatic-logging' anchor.
Pulumi has a Community Slack at slack.pulumi.com that provides community support.
Pulumi offers paid support options.
A guide for filing GitHub issues exists at /docs/support/filing-issues/.

The related pages exist at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/troubleshooting/, /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/editing-state-files/, restoring-deleted-stacks/, targeted-updates/, /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/, and /docs/iac/operations/debugging/using-dev-builds/.
GitHub issue pulumi/pulumi#20846 relates to the update conflict troubleshooting page, and the #conflict hash redirects to /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/.
GitHub issue pulumi/docs#16985 relates to the verbose logging page, and the #verbose-logging hash redirects to /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/#cli-verbose-logging.
Editing Pulumi state files by hand is safe when using the documented techniques.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the resource providing them has been created or updated.

In Pulumi, converting an output value to a string directly (concatenating, logging) instead of using apply or an equivalent helper does not raise an error by default; it silently substitutes a placeholder message for the value.

In Pulumi TypeScript, the resulting string from converting an Output to a string contains literal text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In Pulumi TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an output, or letting one flow into a JSON body, produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Pulumi Python, converting an Output to a string produces literal text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning.
In Pulumi Python, using an Output in an f-string produces a broken string and logs a warning, with no exception raised.
In Pulumi Python, passing an Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`; `Output.json_dumps()` should be used instead.
Pulumi Python provides `Output.json_dumps()` for serializing outputs to JSON.
In Pulumi Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error, so static typing generally prevents the toString mistake.
In Pulumi Go, output values are resolved with `ApplyT`.
In Pulumi C#, converting an Output to a string produces literal text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` (supported in TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes converting an Output to a string throw an exception at the point of the mistake instead of returning the placeholder text.

With the toString-on-Output mistake, the Pulumi program runs and `pulumi up` succeeds, and the placeholder text only surfaces later in a log line, generated config file, or downstream resource property.

Pulumi provides string-composition helpers for outputs: `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript, `Output.concat`/`Output.format`/`Output.json_dumps` in Python, `pulumi.Sprintf`/`pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go, and `Output.Format` in C#.

A value read inside a Pulumi `apply` callback is only available inside that callback (or in outputs derived from it); assigning it to an outer variable and using it outside the callback yields undefined because the callback runs asynchronously after top-level program code has finished.
The Pulumi `apply` callback runs when the engine resolves the dependency graph, not on the program's clock, so adding a delay does not fix reading the outer variable.

Most Pulumi resource inputs accept Outputs as well as plain values, so passing an Output directly (e.g. `bucket: bucket.bucketName`) to a resource works without apply and lets Pulumi resolve the dependency.
A handful of positions in a Pulumi program, such as a resource's logical name, cannot accept an output.

In dynamically typed languages, an `if` on a Pulumi Output evaluates the output object itself rather than its eventual value, so the condition is generally always true; in statically typed languages this is usually a compile error because an `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.
Values known when a Pulumi program starts, such as stack configuration read with `pulumi.Config`, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values and can be branched on normally.
When a branch depends on a resource's output in Pulumi, the branch must move inside `apply`, e.g. `vpc.vpcId.apply((id) => (id.startsWith("vpc-0") ? 3 : 6))` derives a new Output.
Passing a Pulumi Output as a resource's logical name, loop bound, or map key fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#, where these positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In Pulumi Python, passing an output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Pulumi Python, using an output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Pulumi Python, using an output as a dictionary key does not raise an error; Python falls back to comparing and hashing the output object itself, so the lookup silently keys on the wrong thing.

Resource names or counts depending on data only known after resource creation can be handled by restructuring dependent resources into a separate, later stack that consumes the first stack's outputs through a StackReference.

Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and pull a resolved value out of an output synchronously; trying to await or read an output synchronously either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.

Pulumi does not allow synchronously reading output values because doing so would defeat building the dependency graph up front, since the engine would need the value before determining the creation order.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
A StackReference from another Pulumi program consumes one stack's outputs as another stack's inputs.
The Pulumi Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (for example `res.Outputs` in Go).
Pulumi's treatment of resource properties as Outputs is central to how Pulumi builds a dependency graph and runs `pulumi preview`.

Documentation pages exist at /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/#outputs, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/, /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences, and /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
